polityNote: Kingdom of Bhutan, the twenty dzongkhags. Atoms: geoBoundaries ADM2 of BTN (205 gewogs, OCHA ROAP, CC BY 3.0 IGO). A dzongkhag is the union of the gewogs the Election Commission lists for it (Wikipedia «Gewogs of Bhutan», rev 1342287013); the geoBoundaries ADM1 (a 2010 Wikimedia map, coarser than the gewogs and dated before the 2007 transfer) served only to group the gewogs, and 16 gewogs where it disagreed with the list follow the list. ① Each dzongkhag holds the number of gewogs the list gives (205 in all). Against the areas in the Wikipedia infoboxes (several cite the National Statistics Bureau, 2010) the gewog unions agree within 1% for Chhukha 1,883/1,880 km², Dagana 1,726/1,713, Gasa 3,139/3,118, Punakha 1,111/1,110, Samtse 1,307/1,305, Trashiyangtse 1,451/1,438 and Tsirang 639/639; Sarpang 1,658 against 1,946 is the 2007 transfer (the three gewogs add 336 km²); Thimphu 1,799/2,067, Wangdue Phodrang 4,042/4,308 and Trashigang 2,206/3,066 differ, and statoids notes that its two sources for dzongkhag areas differ by up to 50% and add up to more than the country, so these are not read as a different line.

sources.title: Statoids: Districts of Bhutan (Gwillim Law)
sources.says: Bhutan has twenty dzongkhag; 1992: Gasa split from Punakha and Tashi Yangtse from Tashigang, other district boundaries changed.

unresolved.why: Statoids records that in 1992 «other district boundaries changed» besides the creation of Gasa and Trashiyangtse without saying which; between 2002 and 2005 gewogs were dissolved and created (199 → 205) and in 2007 three gewogs moved from Sarpang to Dagana, which statoids does not list — so the change list is incomplete, and no source gives the gewog-by-dzongkhag list before 2007 to show that today’s gewog lines carried the 1992–2007 dzongkhag lines.
checked: Wikipedia Gewogs of Bhutan rev 1342287013 (Gewog changes since 2000)
unresolved.needs: the gewog list per dzongkhag of 1992 and 2002 (Planning Commission / Department of Local Governance) with the 2002–2005 gewog splits as atoms
